population: Ten new text inputs across five previously studied static ELF programs and two earlier controls (Scrivener/distant_versions, Wall/crossed_intervals). Generate inputs and compute independent expected outputs before profiling. Every row is held out of calibration on other inputs.
baseline: After each complete exact-input profile, record the first direct native user plus system CPU observation on the same pinned CPU and boot. Calibrate the deterministic work clock with this measurement.
candidate: Finish every profile and its baseline observation before the rounds. Sort all cases by SHA-256 of the case_id UTF-8 bytes. Make three full additional native calibration rounds, rotating the start by 0, 1 and 2 positions respectively; each case receives one observation per round on CPU 1. Select the middle of these three observations ordered by CPU time, breaking ties chronologically. Use the normal work-clock policy of the selected exact-input measurement for every limit on that input. Record all three extra native payments. Never transfer a scale across inputs or boots.
enforcement: After the three rounds, alternate the first live arm by preregistered case index plus deadline index. Run both clocks on each distinct limit from the union of fixed 5, 12, 25, 50 ms (also 13 ms for the repeated Scrivener input) and ceil(85%, 100%, 115% of that boot's first exact-input native estimate in whole ms). Use a separate 120-second wall watchdog.
reference: After all live decisions, run eleven independent direct wait4 native rounds in case_id digest order with start offsets 0 through 10 modulo case count, all on CPU 1, one thread per core. Compare each observed result with unanimous and majority votes from that input. Equality with the whole-ms limit is within budget.
evaluation: Rerun the identical payload on two new AMD Milan GCE boots. The primary endpoint is median absolute relative error against the independent native median over the ten prospectively registered inputs per boot. Evaluate each boot separately. Report each arm's maximum and signed errors, paired input wins/ties/losses, fixed and all-limit unanimous and majority agreement, per-input costs, and each boot's two earlier controls separately. Compare identical fixed deadlines across boots; adaptive limits are host-local. Duration improvement and live verdict accuracy are separate outcomes.
